newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait refinery to get $23mln control room.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait refinery to get $23mln control room.

text.p: Kuwait's 200,000 barrel per day Shuaiba refinery will complete a $23 million control room modernisation project by 1999, industry executives said.

U.S. firms Pritchard Corp and Black & Veatch were named earlier this year main contractors for the project. Honeywell Inc was awarded a subcontract to build the main control system while electrical and civil subcontracts are still pending.

The Kuwait National Petroleum Co (KNPC) Shuaiba refinery, which last year underwent turnaround maintenance, was scheduled to have a Honeywell control system on line in October 1990 -- two months after the Iraqi invasion of the oil-rich Gulf Arab state.
"After (1991) liberation we discovered that the system, which was tested and stored, was stolen by the Iraqis who sold it in East Europe," said one executive of the project.
Industry sources said Shuaiba had no maintenance planned for this year but will have a general shutdown for major work in 2000.

OPEC member Kuwait has a two million bpd quota and a refining capacity at home of about 895,000 bpd. It has a refining and downstream network in Europe and plans to build a similar one in the growing energy markets of Asia.
